relevance_note: An experimental intravital-microscopy study of neutrophils from one identifiable LAD-I patient: "one with LAD type 1 (LAD-I; patient 1 in reference 17)".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory, spans checked verbatim by script. In scope: the single LAD-I (CD18-deficient) patient, previously published as 'patient 1 in reference 17' (Bowen et al. 1982). Out of scope (no rows): the LAD-II patient (normal CD18, fucosylation defect; 'patient 1 in reference 19') and the two healthy donors; cohort_size_as_stated = 2 patients. Label chosen by rule 4 ('ref 17 patient') because the paper itself uses only the role phrase 'the LAD-I patient' and 'patient 1' is the earlier paper's label (also used for the LAD-II patient of ref 19). The patient is studied first-hand (ex vivo/in vivo neutrophil experiments), so source_reference_in_review is 'not reported'; the earlier report is recorded in publications.prior_report_citation. No ITGB2 variant, gene symbol or zygosity is printed; the paper only says LAD-I is 'An inherited defect in the synthesis of CD18', so no variants row was created. Phenotypic rows are laboratory/functional findings on the patient's neutrophils (CD18 absent, ~50% less L-selectin, normal sLe*, normal rolling, failure to stick on LTB4); normal findings recorded as the excluded abnormality per D-27. No clinical features are given for this patient; the general statement that LAD patients have infections without pus despite elevated leukocyte counts is about the disease, not this person, so all 20 checklist items are 'not reported'. No contradictions found. Neutrophil experiments were done in rabbit mesentery venules (human neutrophils injected into rabbits).
